CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Limitation of Liability
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Caps and excludes categories of damages.

sub_elements.name: Aggregate liability cap
sub_elements.description: Numerical or formulaic cap on total damages.

sub_elements.name: Exclusion of consequential damages
sub_elements.description: Excludes indirect, incidental, special, consequential, lost profits.

sub_elements.name: Carveouts
sub_elements.description: Categories not subject to cap (indemnity, IP infringement, gross negligence, fraud, breach of confidentiality).

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, (A) IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, LOST REVENUE, OR LOSS OF DATA, AND (B) EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO PROVIDER UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.
regex_anchors: in no event shall (?:either|any) party be liable

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Indemnification

sub_elements.name: Scope of indemnified claims
sub_elements.description: Categories: IP infringement, breach, negligence, etc.

sub_elements.name: Indemnification procedure
sub_elements.description: Notice, control of defense, cooperation, settlement consent.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Each party ("Indemnitor") shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other party and its officers, directors, employees, and agents ("Indemnitees") from and against any third-party claims, suits, or proceedings, and all related losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) Indemnitor's breach of this Agreement, (b) the gross negligence or willful misconduct of Indemnitor, or (c) the infringement of any third-party intellectual property right by Indemnitor's deliverables. Indemnitee shall (i) promptly notify Indemnitor in writing of the claim, (ii) give Indemnitor sole control of the defense and settlement, and (iii) provide reasonable cooperation at Indemnitor's expense. Indemnitor shall not settle any claim that imposes liability or admission on Indemnitee without Indemnitee's prior written consent.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Warranty Disclaimer
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, THE SERVICES ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE," AND PROVIDER DISCLAIMS ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, OR STATUTORY, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, AND NON-INFRINGEMENT.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: IP Assignment

sub_elements.name: Scope of assignment
sub_elements.description: Deliverables, work product, related IP rights.

sub_elements.name: Moral rights waiver
sub_elements.description: Waiver to extent permitted by law.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Provider hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to the Deliverables and any derivative works thereof. To the extent any such rights cannot be assigned by law, Provider hereby grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute such rights. Provider waives any moral rights in the Deliverables to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: IP License Grant
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Grant of license rights to IP.
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Licensor hereby grants to Licensee a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, worldwide, royalty-free license, during the Term, to use the Licensed IP solely for Licensee's internal business purposes.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Feedback License
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: License-back of customer feedback to provider.

sub_elements.name: No obligation to use
sub_elements.description: Provider has no duty to act on feedback.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Customer grants Provider a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license to use, modify, and incorporate any feedback, suggestions, or recommendations Customer provides regarding the Services into Provider's products and services without any obligation or attribution to Customer.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Confidentiality

sub_elements.name: Standard exclusions
sub_elements.description: Public, independently developed, lawfully received, required by law.

sub_elements.name: Duration of confidentiality obligation
sub_elements.description: Often N years post-termination, or perpetual for trade secrets.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: "Confidential Information" means any non-public information disclosed by one party ("Discloser") to the other ("Recipient"), whether orally or in writing, that is designated as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no breach of this Agreement; (b) was known to Recipient prior to disclosure; (c) is received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed by Recipient without reference to the Confidential Information. Recipient shall protect Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but no less than reasonable care, for a period of three (3) years following disclosure (or, for trade secrets, for so long as such information remains a trade secret under applicable law). If compelled by law to disclose, Recipient shall give Discloser prompt notice and reasonable cooperation, at Discloser's expense, in seeking a protective order.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Term
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Initial and renewal term of the agreement.

sub_elements.name: Renewal mechanism
sub_elements.description: Auto-renew vs. mutual renewal vs. fixed.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for an initial term of one (1) year (the "Initial Term"). Thereafter, this Agreement will automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms (each, a "Renewal Term") unless either party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Termination for Convenience
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience by providing the other party with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Termination for Cause
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Termination on material breach with cure period.

sub_elements.name: Cure period
sub_elements.description: Days to cure after written notice.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other party (a) materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail, or (b) becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, files or has filed against it a petition in bankruptcy, or has a receiver appointed.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Effects of Termination

sub_elements.name: Refund of prepaid fees
sub_elements.description: Whether prepaid amounts are refunded on termination by customer for cause.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement: (a) all rights and licenses granted hereunder shall immediately terminate; (b) each party shall promptly return or destroy the other party's Confidential Information and certify such destruction in writing upon request; and (c) the following sections shall survive: Confidentiality, Indemnification, Limitation of Liability, and Governing Law. If Customer terminates for Provider's uncured material breach, Provider shall refund any prepaid, unused fees on a pro-rata basis.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Payment Terms
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Invoicing, due dates, late fees, taxes.

sub_elements.name: Taxes allocation
sub_elements.description: Customer typically responsible for sales/use tax.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days of receipt of invoice. Late payments shall accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law. All fees are exclusive of taxes, and Customer is responsible for all applicable sales, use, and similar taxes (excluding taxes on Provider's income). Customer must give written notice of any disputed amount within fifteen (15) days of the invoice date and the parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Price Increase / Adjustment

sub_elements.name: Notice period
sub_elements.description: Advance notice before increase takes effect.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Provider may increase fees at the start of any Renewal Term by no more than the greater of (a) five percent (5%) or (b) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index (All Urban Consumers) for the prior twelve-month period, provided that Provider gives Customer at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice of any such increase.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Data Security

sub_elements.name: Encryption in transit and at rest

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Provider shall maintain a written information security program containing administrative, technical, and physical safeguards consistent with industry standards (such as ISO/IEC 27001 or SOC 2 Type II). Provider shall encrypt all Customer Data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256 or an equivalent standard. Provider shall notify Customer in writing without undue delay, and in no event later than seventy-two (72) hours, after becoming aware of any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Privacy / DPA Reference
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: To the extent Provider Processes Personal Data on behalf of Customer, the parties' Data Processing Addendum, available at [URL] ("DPA"), is incorporated by reference and forms part of this Agreement. Where transfers of Personal Data from the EEA, UK, or Switzerland to a third country are involved, the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two) and any applicable UK/Swiss addenda are incorporated and shall apply.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Governing Law

sub_elements.name: Conflict-of-laws principles excluded
sub_elements.description: 'without regard to its conflict of laws principles'.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Venue / Forum Selection

sub_elements.name: Specific courts named
sub_elements.description: State and federal courts in named county.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Each party irrevocably consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of, and venue in, the state and federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection based on inconvenient forum.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Arbitration

sub_elements.name: IP / equitable relief carveout
sub_elements.description: Court relief for IP and injunctions preserved.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement that the parties cannot resolve through good-faith negotiation within thirty (30) days shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS pursuant to its Comprehensive Arbitration Rules, by a single arbitrator. The seat of arbitration shall be New York, New York, and the language of the arbitration shall be English. Each party waives any right to participate in a class, collective, or representative action. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property or confidential information.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Jury Trial Waiver
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION OR PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Non-Compete

sub_elements.name: Independent consideration
sub_elements.description: Required in some states (e.g., NC, TX).

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Recipient shall not, directly or indirectly, within the United States, engage in any business that competes with the specific products or services Recipient had material involvement with under this Agreement.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Non-Solicitation

sub_elements.name: General advertising carveout
sub_elements.description: Exclusion for general public hiring efforts.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall, directly or indirectly, solicit for employment any employee of the other party with whom it had material contact in connection with this Agreement; provided that general advertising not directed at such employees shall not be a violation of this Section.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Assignment
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may assign this Agreement, upon written notice and without consent, to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, corporate reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section is void.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Force Majeure
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Excuse for performance during specified events.

sub_elements.name: Covered events
sub_elements.description: Acts of God, war, pandemic, etc.

sub_elements.name: Termination right after extended event
sub_elements.description: After N days of continued event.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance under this Agreement (other than payment obligations) due to causes beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil disturbance, pandemic, governmental order, or failure of public utilities or the Internet. The affected party shall give prompt notice and use reasonable efforts to resume performance. If a force majeure event continues for more than thirty (30) days, the non-affected party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Entire Agreement / Integration
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties regarding its subject matter and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous agreements, understandings, and communications, whether written or oral. No modification or amendment to this Agreement is binding unless in a writing signed by an authorized representative of each party.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Severability
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Invalidation of one provision does not invalidate the rest.
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, and the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Notices
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: How and where notices are sent.
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and shall be deemed given (a) upon receipt when delivered personally or by nationally recognized overnight courier, (b) on the third business day after deposit with the U.S. Postal Service, certified mail, return receipt requested, or (c) on confirmation of receipt when sent by email to the addresses specified on the signature page or such other address as a party may designate by notice.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Audit Rights
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, but not more than once per twelve-month period (except for cause), Customer or its independent auditor may, during normal business hours and subject to reasonable confidentiality obligations, audit Provider's books and records solely to verify compliance with this Agreement. Customer shall bear the cost of the audit unless it reveals an underpayment or material non-compliance, in which case Provider shall reimburse the reasonable audit costs.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Publicity
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.description: Use of name / logo / case studies.
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Neither party shall issue any press release or public statement, or use the other party's name, trademarks, or logos, without the other party's prior written consent.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Insurance

sub_elements.name: Types of coverage
sub_elements.description: CGL, E&O, cyber, workers comp, etc.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Provider shall maintain, at its sole cost, the following insurance during the term: (a) Commercial General Liability with limits of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate; (b) Professional Liability / Errors & Omissions of at least $2,000,000 per claim; (c) Cyber / Technology E&O of at least $5,000,000 per claim; and (d) Workers' Compensation as required by law. Provider shall name Customer as additional insured (other than for workers' compensation and professional liability) and provide certificates of insurance upon request.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Export Controls / Sanctions

sub_elements.name: Embargoed-country certification
sub_elements.description: Customer certifies it is not in a sanctioned country.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Each party shall comply with all applicable export control and sanctions laws and regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations and the regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control. Customer represents that it is not located in, organized under the laws of, or ordinarily resident in any country or region subject to comprehensive U.S. sanctions, and is not on any U.S. restricted-party list.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Anti-Corruption
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: Each party shall comply with all applicable anti-corruption laws, including the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the U.K. Bribery Act, and shall not, directly or indirectly, offer, promise, or give anything of value to any government official or other person to improperly influence any act or decision.

CANONICAL_CLAUSES.name: Counterparts
CANONICAL_CLAUSES.market_standard_text: This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures delivered by electronic means (including DocuSign or similar services) shall have the same legal effect as original signatures.

authorities.cite: Edwards v. Arthur Andersen LLP, 44 Cal. 4th 937 (2008)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: California voids most non-competes, including narrow ones; only sale-of-business and entity-dissolution exceptions apply.
JURISDICTION_RULES.recommended_text: [Non-compete intentionally omitted — unenforceable in California under Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16600. Use confidentiality and non-solicit-of-customers obligations only.]

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: North Dakota statutorily voids most non-competes, with limited sale-of-business exception.
Oklahoma generally voids non-competes; allows narrow non-solicit of established customers.
Minnesota voids new employee non-competes entered into on/after July 1, 2023.

authorities.cite: Marsh USA Inc. v. Cook, 354 S.W.3d 764 (Tex. 2011)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: Texas requires the non-compete be ancillary to an otherwise enforceable agreement and reasonable in scope, time, and geography. Courts may reform overbroad covenants.
Florida is one of the most employer-friendly states; the statute sets rebuttable presumptions of reasonableness by duration (not hard caps) and authorizes modification.
Massachusetts requires garden leave (min 50% base salary) or other mutually agreed consideration plus written notice with right to counsel.

Washington requires earnings thresholds, advance disclosure, and presumes a duration over 18 months unreasonable. The earnings thresholds are adjusted every year; the figures recorded here are the 2024 amounts — verify the current figure.

authorities.cite: Illinois Freedom to Work Act, 820 ILCS 90

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: Illinois requires an income threshold for non-competes ($75k when the Act took effect; the statute raises it on a schedule — verify the current figure), 14 days advance review, and either continued employment for 2+ years or other adequate consideration.

authorities.cite: Tristate Courier & Carriage, Inc. v. Berryman, 2004 WL 835886 (Del. Ch.)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: Delaware enforces reasonable non-competes; Chancery Court may blue-pencil overbroad scope.
New York's BDO Seidman three-prong test: legitimate interest, no undue hardship, not injurious to public.

authorities.cite: AMN Healthcare, Inc. v. Aya Healthcare Services, Inc., 28 Cal. App. 5th 923 (2018)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: California treats employee non-solicits as void post-AMN; customer non-solicits void unless protecting actual trade secrets.
Texas treats non-solicits like non-competes — must be reasonable and ancillary.

authorities.cite: Grafton Partners L.P. v. Superior Court, 36 Cal. 4th 944 (2005)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: California voids pre-dispute contractual jury waivers; arbitration is the alternative.

authorities.cite: Bank S., N.A. v. Howard, 264 Ga. 339 (1994)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: Georgia generally voids contractual pre-dispute jury waivers.
Delaware enforces conspicuous, knowing, voluntary jury waivers.
New York enforces jury waivers if knowing and voluntary; conspicuousness matters.

authorities.cite: In re Prudential Ins. Co. of Am., 148 S.W.3d 124 (Tex. 2004)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: Texas Supreme Court enforces knowing/voluntary waivers.

authorities.cite: Armendariz v. Foundation Health Psychcare Servs., Inc., 24 Cal. 4th 83 (2000)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: California requires Armendariz factors for employment arbitration; PAGA representative claims cannot be fully waived.

authorities.cite: Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act of 2021 (9 U.S.C. § 402)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: Federal law makes pre-dispute arbitration of sexual-harassment/assault claims unenforceable at the claimant's election.

authorities.cite: Kalisch-Jarcho, Inc. v. City of New York, 58 N.Y.2d 377 (1983)

JURISDICTION_RULES.note: New York voids contractual limitations on liability for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud — these must be carved out.
California voids contracts exempting parties from responsibility for willful injury or violation of law (whether willful or negligent).
Under the UCC, disclaimers of merchantability must mention the word 'merchantability' and be conspicuous (typically all-caps).
Delaware enforces choice-of-Delaware-law in commercial contracts of $100k+ even without minimum contacts.
